poverty_rate.name: Overall Poverty Headcount Rate (%)
poverty_rate.source_document: KNBS (2020) Comprehensive Poverty Report, p. 12 & KNBS (2023) Kenya Poverty Report
poverty_rate.official_definition: The proportion of the population whose monthly adult equivalent consumption expenditure falls below the national overall poverty line (KSh 3,252 per adult equivalent per month for rural areas and KSh 5,995 for urban areas in 2015/16 prices, rebased to 2019).
poverty_rate.numerator: Number of individuals living in households with monthly adult equivalent consumption below the statutory poverty line.
poverty_rate.directionality_rationale: Poverty rate measures economic deprivation. Higher values reflect greater deprivation, lower liquid asset reserves, and heightened vulnerability to climatic shocks.
poverty_rate.climate_relevance: Drought shocks cause rapid entitlement collapse in high-poverty pastoralist households lacking cash buffers or credit access.
poverty_rate.guidance: Proposals must prioritize emergency unconditional cash transfers, subsidized index-based livestock insurance (KLIP), and community-level savings schemes.

extreme_poverty.name: Extreme (Food) Poverty Headcount (%)
extreme_poverty.official_definition: The proportion of individuals whose adult equivalent consumption expenditure on food is less than the minimum required food basket to meet the recommended daily dietary allowance of 2,250 kilocalories (KSh 1,954 per adult equivalent per month in rural areas and KSh 2,551 in urban areas).
extreme_poverty.numerator: Individuals whose food spending fails to secure 2,250 kcal/day.
extreme_poverty.directionality_rationale: Measures acute nutritional subsistence failure. Higher rates indicate immediate food crisis vulnerability.
extreme_poverty.climate_relevance: Seasonal rain failure triggers immediate household caloric deficits within 3–4 weeks in ASAL rangelands.
extreme_poverty.guidance: Pre-position therapeutic nutrition rations and expand universal school feeding programs during Alert/Alarm drought phases.

mpi_index.name: Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)
mpi_index.source_document: KNBS (2020) Comprehensive Poverty Report: Multidimensional Deprivation in Kenya, p. 24
mpi_index.official_definition: Measures the incidence and intensity of simultaneous deprivations experienced by individuals across essential dimensions: physical infrastructure, housing conditions, education, health, and economic well-being, calculated using the Alkire-Foster method.
mpi_index.numerator: Weighted sum of deprived dimensions experienced by deprived households.
mpi_index.denominator: Total population multiplied by total dimensions evaluated.
mpi_index.directionality_rationale: Higher MPI values signify compounded, overlapping deprivations across multiple social and economic spheres.
mpi_index.climate_relevance: Overlapping deprivations prevent pastoralists from adopting standalone technological coping strategies.
mpi_index.guidance: Deploy bundled, multi-sectoral resilience packages combining solar water, clean energy, and mobile health outreach.

vulnerable_employment.name: Vulnerable Employment Rate (%)
vulnerable_employment.source_document: KNBS (2019) Kenya Population and Housing Census Volume IV: Socio-Economic Characteristics, Table 2.18
vulnerable_employment.official_definition: The proportion of the employed population working as own-account workers or contributing family workers, characterized by job informality, low productivity, and complete lack of formal social protection.
vulnerable_employment.numerator: Employed persons classified as own-account or contributing family workers.
vulnerable_employment.directionality_rationale: High vulnerable employment reflects lack of formal contracts, severance, or insurance to absorb covariate climate impacts.
vulnerable_employment.climate_relevance: Pastoral subsistence labor collapses during multi-season droughts, leaving youth without alternative income.
vulnerable_employment.guidance: Support community savings and loan associations (VSLAs), pasture reseeding micro-enterprises, and commercial fodder value chains.

youth_neet.name: Youth NEET Rate (15–24) (%)
youth_neet.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 5 & p. 9
youth_neet.official_definition: Percentage of the population of a given age group (15-24 years) not employed and not involved in further education or training. Numerator refers to persons meeting two conditions: not employed (unemployed or inactive by ILO definition) and have not received any formal or non-formal education or training in the four weeks preceding the survey.
youth_neet.numerator: Persons aged 15–24 not in employment and not in education or training.
youth_neet.denominator: Total population aged 15–24 excluding unstated responses.
youth_neet.directionality_rationale: Higher rates signify idle youth disconnected from human capital accumulation, increasing vulnerability to distress coping.
youth_neet.climate_relevance: Unoccupied pastoralist youth face heightened pressure to engage in distress asset sales or resource conflicts during droughts.
youth_neet.guidance: Fund vocational training in solar borehole maintenance, leather processing, and climate-resilient water infrastructure construction.

cash_transfer_cov.name: Social Cash Transfer Coverage (HSNP) (%)
cash_transfer_cov.source_document: State Department for Social Protection / KNBS (2022) Kenya Continuous Household Survey
cash_transfer_cov.official_definition: Proportion of vulnerable households actively enrolled in statutory national safety net cash transfer programs (Hunger Safety Net Programme - HSNP, Inua Jamii).
cash_transfer_cov.numerator: Households with active biometric enrollment in national safety net cash transfers.
cash_transfer_cov.directionality_rationale: Higher coverage provides an established, rapid digital cash payment highway for anticipatory early action.
cash_transfer_cov.climate_relevance: Existing bank and biometric infrastructure enables immediate emergency horizontal scale-up prior to peak hazard impacts.
cash_transfer_cov.guidance: Link seasonal forecast triggers directly to HSNP Group 2 emergency top-up payment protocols.

clean_cooking.name: Clean Cooking Energy Access (%)
clean_cooking.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 4 & p. 6
clean_cooking.official_definition: Proportion of households by primary reliance on clean fuels and technologies for cooking, space heating, and lighting (LPG, electricity, biogas, solar, and improved ethanol stoves).
clean_cooking.numerator: Households using clean fuels as primary cooking technology.
clean_cooking.denominator: Total private households in the county.
clean_cooking.directionality_rationale: Higher access improves household respiratory health and halts local deforestation around water catchment towers.
clean_cooking.climate_relevance: Over-reliance on firewood accelerates degradation of cloud forests (e.g., Mount Marsabit, Mount Kulal) critical for dryland recharge.
clean_cooking.guidance: Promote energy-efficient institutional biomass cookstoves and community biogas digesters to alleviate female firewood burdens.

open_defecation.name: Open Defecation / Unimproved Sanitation (%)
open_defecation.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 4 (Sanitation ladder) & 2019 KPHC Vol IV
open_defecation.official_definition: Distribution of de jure population by sanitation service ladder: proportion of population practicing open defecation (disposal of human feces in fields, bushes, water bodies, or other open spaces) rather than basic or improved sanitation facilities.
open_defecation.numerator: Population reporting open defecation as sanitation practice.
open_defecation.directionality_rationale: Higher open defecation rates correlate with severe fecal water contamination and waterborne disease outbreaks.
open_defecation.climate_relevance: Flash floods and heavy rains rapidly flush surface human waste into unprotected water pans and shallow wells, triggering cholera epidemics.
open_defecation.guidance: Construct flood-resilient raised VIP latrines at public livestock watering points and pre-position water chlorination tablets.

female_headship.name: Female-Headed Households (%)
female_headship.source_document: KNBS (2019) Kenya Population and Housing Census Volume IV: Socio-Economic Characteristics, p. 6 & Table 2.11
female_headship.official_definition: Household Head: Defined by KNBS as the most responsible or respected member of the household (as at the census night) who makes key decisions in the household on a day to day basis, and whose authority is recognized by all members of the household. Female-headed household represents the proportion of private households where the designated head is female.
female_headship.numerator: Number of private households headed by a female.
female_headship.denominator: Total enumerated private households in the county.
female_headship.directionality_rationale: Household headship is a structural demographic classification describing family living arrangements, not an intrinsic defect or advantage. Under international (UN Statistics Division) and national (KNBS) demographic standards, higher female headship is neither positive nor negative. It reflects diverse socio-economic dynamics including adult male circular labor migration, marital patterns, widowhood, or female autonomy. Classifying female headship as an 'adverse vulnerability deficit' is conceptually invalid. For climate adaptation, headship data guides gender-responsive, non-exclusionary targeting (ensuring female-headed households receive direct asset restocking and early warnings) rather than stigmatizing household structure.
female_headship.climate_relevance: Female pastoralist household heads often face distinct institutional barriers under customary clan rangeland governance councils (Dedha) and own smaller livestock herds.
female_headship.guidance: Mandate at least 50% female representation on local disaster risk management committees and ring-fence small-ruminant restocking and micro-credit directly for female heads.

teen_pregnancy.name: Adolescent Pregnancy Rate (15–19) (%)
teen_pregnancy.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 5 & p. 7
teen_pregnancy.official_definition: Percent of women age 15-19 who have ever been pregnant (have had a live birth, are currently pregnant with first child, or have experienced a pregnancy loss). Numerator: number of women age 15-19 ever been pregnant. Denominator: Number of women age 15-19.
teen_pregnancy.numerator: Number of women age 15–19 who have ever been pregnant.
teen_pregnancy.denominator: Total women age 15–19 in the county.
teen_pregnancy.directionality_rationale: Higher rates severely curtail educational and economic attainment for young women and elevate maternal and infant health risks.
teen_pregnancy.climate_relevance: Prolonged droughts increase economic distress, leading to negative coping strategies including transactional sex and early marriage for livestock bride-price.
teen_pregnancy.guidance: Incorporate girl-child secondary school retention bursaries and emergency dignity kits into county contingency emergency plans.

early_marriage.name: Child / Early Marriage (<18) (%)
early_marriage.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 4 & p. 7
early_marriage.official_definition: Prevalence of child marriage: the proportion of females (and males) age 20-24 who were married or in a union before reaching the statutory age of 18 years.
early_marriage.directionality_rationale: Violates child protection statutes and perpetuates intergenerational gender inequality and educational marginalization.
early_marriage.climate_relevance: Drought-induced livestock asset collapse pressures destitute families to marry off young daughters to restock camel and cattle herds.
early_marriage.guidance: Couple emergency safety-net cash transfers with strict school attendance retention conditions for adolescent pastoralist girls.

female_literacy.name: Female Adult Literacy Rate (%)
female_literacy.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 8
female_literacy.official_definition: Literacy by sex: proportion of women age 15-49 who can read all or part of a sentence in English, Kiswahili, or any local language.
female_literacy.numerator: Women age 15–49 demonstrating basic reading competence.
female_literacy.denominator: Total women age 15–49 tested in the survey.
female_literacy.directionality_rationale: Higher literacy enhances access to early warning bulletins, financial services, and civic decision-making.
female_literacy.climate_relevance: Low literacy prevents female pastoralists from receiving or comprehending standard SMS early warning alerts and advisories.
female_literacy.guidance: Disseminate seasonal weather outlooks through vernacular community FM radio (Borana, Rendille, Gabbra) and illustrated voice messaging.

male_literacy.name: Male Adult Literacy Rate (%)
male_literacy.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 8
male_literacy.official_definition: Literacy by sex: proportion of men age 15-49 who can read all or part of a sentence in English, Kiswahili, or any local language.
male_literacy.numerator: Men age 15–49 demonstrating basic reading competence.
male_literacy.denominator: Total men age 15–49 tested in the survey.
male_literacy.directionality_rationale: Higher literacy improves adoption of scientific early warning information and formal livestock marketing channels.
male_literacy.climate_relevance: Low literacy reinforces reliance on traditional weather prognosticators over scientific meteorological forecasts.
male_literacy.guidance: Facilitate structured consensus workshops between traditional rangeland elders and KMD County Directors of Meteorology.

female_secondary.name: Female Secondary School Completion (%)
female_secondary.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 8 & p. 9
female_secondary.official_definition: Educational attainment: proportion of females age 18 and above who have attended or completed secondary school education.
female_secondary.denominator: Total female population age 18 and older.
female_secondary.directionality_rationale: Secondary education is the single most powerful driver of livelihood diversification and female adaptive capacity.
female_secondary.climate_relevance: Restricts women from formal employment and non-pastoral economic diversification during prolonged drought cycles.
female_secondary.guidance: Provide vocational technical trade bursaries and green business incubation grants targeted at pastoralist young women.

female_land_title.name: Female Sole Land Ownership (%)
female_land_title.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 4 & p. 9
female_land_title.official_definition: House and land ownership by sex: percentage of women age 15-49 who own agricultural or non-agricultural land alone with title or deed.
female_land_title.numerator: Women owning registered land solely in their own name.
female_land_title.denominator: Total women age 15–49 in the survey.
female_land_title.directionality_rationale: Land title provides legal security of tenure and functions as collateral required for commercial agricultural bank credit.
female_land_title.climate_relevance: Lack of land title prevents women from investing in capital-intensive land conservation and irrigation structures.
female_land_title.guidance: Structure adaptation micro-credit lines using group-based social collateral guarantees for women-led producer cooperatives.

female_livestock_owner.name: Female Sole Livestock Ownership (%)
female_livestock_owner.official_definition: Proportion of women age 15-49 who have independent ownership and commercial disposal rights over livestock herds (cattle, camels, sheep, goats).
female_livestock_owner.numerator: Women with independent legal/customary livestock ownership.
female_livestock_owner.denominator: Total adult women in pastoralist households.
female_livestock_owner.directionality_rationale: Livestock is the primary capital asset in ASALs; independent ownership empowers women to execute timely destocking.
female_livestock_owner.climate_relevance: Commercial cattle/camel sales are controlled by men, delaying critical destocking ahead of severe drought mortality.
female_livestock_owner.guidance: Center adaptation interventions on dairy goat breed improvement, poultry hubs, and camel milk cooperatives where women retain control.

female_decision_making.name: Female Financial Decision Autonomy (%)
female_decision_making.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 5 & p. 9
female_decision_making.official_definition: Women’s participation in decision making: percent distribution of currently married women age 15-49 who make decisions alone or jointly with their husband on: own healthcare, major household purchases, and visits to family or relatives.
female_decision_making.numerator: Married women participating in major household financial decisions.
female_decision_making.directionality_rationale: High decision autonomy enables timely household reallocations of labor and capital during impending climate emergencies.
female_decision_making.climate_relevance: Women are primary managers of household food reserves; delayed joint decision-making impedes early destocking.
female_decision_making.guidance: Conduct gender-transformative household dialogue sessions alongside seasonal climate early warning broadcasts.

gbv_seeking.name: GBV Help-Seeking Access (%)
gbv_seeking.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 4 & p. 10
gbv_seeking.official_definition: Proportion of women age 15-49 who experienced physical or sexual violence and sought help from formal legal, medical, police, or institutional services.
gbv_seeking.denominator: Total women age 15–49 reporting experience of physical or sexual violence.
gbv_seeking.directionality_rationale: Higher reporting reflects availability and trust in institutional protection, healthcare, and judicial systems.
gbv_seeking.climate_relevance: Intimate partner violence spikes during prolonged climate displacement, while remote rangelands lack formal reporting channels.
gbv_seeking.guidance: Establish mobile gender-based violence (GBV) protection desks and dignity spaces at emergency food and water distribution hubs.

improved_water.name: Access to Improved Drinking Water (%)
improved_water.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 3 & p. 6
improved_water.official_definition: Drinking water service ladder (SDG 6.1.1): proportion of population using drinking water from an improved source (piped water, boreholes, protected dug wells, protected springs, rainwater collection).
improved_water.numerator: De jure population accessing drinking water from improved infrastructure.
improved_water.denominator: Total de jure population in the county.
improved_water.directionality_rationale: Higher access safeguards public health, eliminates pathogen ingestion, and reduces water-trekking labor burdens.
improved_water.climate_relevance: Unimproved surface pans dry up first in drought, forcing pastoralist women to dig shallow sand scoots in dry riverbeds.
improved_water.guidance: Drill strategic deep solar-powered boreholes, construct subsurface sand dams, and install community solar water treatment kiosks.

water_distance.name: Dry-Season Water Trekking Distance (km)
water_distance.source_document: KNBS (2019) Kenya Population and Housing Census Volume IV, Section 2
water_distance.official_definition: Average round-trip distance (in kilometers) traveled by household members to fetch drinking water during the dry season.
water_distance.numerator: Cumulative reported round-trip distance to main water source.
water_distance.directionality_rationale: Long water trekking distances exhaust female labor, deplete livestock body condition, and prevent children from attending school.
water_distance.climate_relevance: Water points fail sequentially during severe droughts, forcing daily trekking distances to exceed 20–25 km in North Horr.
water_distance.guidance: Construct strategic water pans along established livestock trek routes and fund emergency motorized water trucking contingencies.

water_time_burden.name: Water Fetching Time Burden (>30m) (%)
water_time_burden.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 3 & p. 6
water_time_burden.official_definition: Drinking water service ladder (limited service): proportion of population who spend more than 30 minutes round-trip collection time to access drinking water.
water_time_burden.numerator: Population spending >30 minutes round-trip fetching water.
water_time_burden.denominator: Total population in households without water on premises.
water_time_burden.directionality_rationale: High time burden falls almost exclusively on women and girls, directly depressing school attendance and economic productivity.
water_time_burden.climate_relevance: During drought, queueing times at motorized boreholes can exceed 6–8 hours daily, exhausting pastoralist women.
water_time_burden.guidance: Siting solar water distribution kiosks within 1.5 km of rural settlements returns 4 to 6 productive hours daily to pastoralist women.

skilled_birth.name: Skilled Birth Attendance Rate (%)
skilled_birth.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 2 & p. 8
skilled_birth.official_definition: Delivery by a skilled provider: proportion of live births attended by skilled health personnel (doctors, nurses, midwives) in an accredited health facility.
skilled_birth.numerator: Deliveries attended by qualified health personnel.
skilled_birth.denominator: Total live births in the 5 years preceding the survey.
skilled_birth.directionality_rationale: Skilled birth delivery directly reduces maternal mortality, obstetric fistulas, and neonatal asphyxia.
skilled_birth.climate_relevance: Flash floods across seasonal luggas completely cut off rural communities from referral hospitals during El Niño inundations.
skilled_birth.guidance: Construct raised masonry drift crossings across vulnerable luggas and establish sub-county maternal waiting homes.

immunization_rate.name: Fully Immunized Child Rate (12–23m) (%)
immunization_rate.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 7 & KDHS 2022
immunization_rate.official_definition: Vaccinations by County: proportion of children age 12-23 months who have received all basic age-appropriate vaccinations (BCG, measles, 3 pentavalent, and 3 oral polio doses).
immunization_rate.numerator: Children 12–23 months with complete statutory vaccination records.
immunization_rate.denominator: Total children age 12–23 months in the survey.
immunization_rate.directionality_rationale: Full immunization provides herd immunity against preventable viral and bacterial epidemics.
immunization_rate.climate_relevance: Nomadic herd migrations cause children to drop out of cold-chain schedules, creating severe measles risk in drought camps.
immunization_rate.guidance: Equip nomadic mobile health outreach teams with solar-direct-drive (SDD) vaccine refrigerators along pastoral migratory corridors.

stunting_rate.name: Under-5 Chronic Stunting Prevalence (%)
stunting_rate.source_document: KNBS (2023) 2022 Kenya Demographic and Health Survey (KDHS), Ch. 11
stunting_rate.official_definition: Nutritional status of children: percentage of children under age 5 whose height-for-age is below minus two standard deviations (-2 SD) from the median of the WHO Child Growth Standards, reflecting chronic undernutrition.
stunting_rate.denominator: Total children under 5 measured in the survey.
stunting_rate.directionality_rationale: Reflects chronic, long-term nutritional deficit causing irreversible cognitive and physical developmental stunting.
stunting_rate.climate_relevance: Repeated drought shocks induce chronic milk deficits, permanently impairing child health and cognitive capital.
stunting_rate.guidance: Promote year-round dryland vegetable kitchen gardens around solar boreholes and distribute fortified supplementary porridge flours.

child_wasting.name: Under-5 Acute Malnutrition (GAM) (%)
child_wasting.official_definition: Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) / Wasting: percentage of children under age 5 whose weight-for-height is below minus two standard deviations (-2 SD) from the median of the WHO Child Growth Standards, reflecting acute nutritional deficit.
child_wasting.numerator: Children under 5 with weight-for-height Z-score < -2 or nutritional edema.
child_wasting.denominator: Total children under 5 measured in the survey.
child_wasting.directionality_rationale: High acute wasting represents an immediate life-threatening emergency requiring therapeutic clinical feeding.
child_wasting.climate_relevance: Breaches WHO emergency thresholds (>15%) when consecutive drought seasons cause dairy herds to migrate away from children.
child_wasting.guidance: Pre-position ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF) and fund mobile supplementary feeding programs upon NDMA Alert phase.

disability_prev.name: Functional Disability Prevalence (%)
disability_prev.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 4 & p. 6
disability_prev.official_definition: Population with a disability: proportion of the de jure population age 15 and over who report difficulty in at least one functional domain (seeing, hearing, communicating, remembering/concentrating, walking/climbing steps, washing/dressing).
disability_prev.numerator: Adults reporting some or severe difficulty in at least one functional domain.
disability_prev.denominator: Total de jure adult population aged 15 and above.
disability_prev.directionality_rationale: Reflects the prevalence of functional impairments requiring dedicated assistive accommodations and emergency support.
disability_prev.climate_relevance: Persons with disabilities face extreme mortality risks during rapid-onset flash floods and emergency herd migrations.
disability_prev.guidance: Integrate disability-inclusive early warning protocols and construct barrier-free emergency evacuation centers.

health_distance.name: Distance to Health Facility (>10 km) (%)
health_distance.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 4 & p. 8
health_distance.official_definition: Problems in accessing healthcare (distance barrier): proportion of population citing physical distance to the nearest health facility (>10 km) as a major obstacle to seeking clinical medical care when ill.
health_distance.numerator: Households residing more than 10 kilometers from the nearest operational dispensary or clinic.
health_distance.denominator: Total enumerated households in the county.
health_distance.directionality_rationale: High physical distance impedes emergency obstetric referrals and prompt treatment of acute diarrheal illnesses.
health_distance.climate_relevance: Floods cut off unpaved roads, isolating remote settlements from healthcare during post-flood malaria outbreaks.
health_distance.guidance: Establish community health volunteer (CHV) networks equipped with solar backpack kits, rapid diagnostics, and oral rehydration salts.

mobile_phone.name: Household Mobile Phone Ownership (%)
mobile_phone.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 9
mobile_phone.official_definition: Proportion of population aged 18+ who own a mobile phone handset, disaggregated by sex.
mobile_phone.numerator: Adults age 18+ reporting personal ownership of a mobile phone.
mobile_phone.denominator: Total adult population age 18+ in the county.
mobile_phone.directionality_rationale: High mobile penetration enables digital early warning dissemination and mobile money cash transfers.
mobile_phone.climate_relevance: Enables automated SMS early warning broadcasts and digital pasture tracking directly to pastoralist herders.
mobile_phone.guidance: Scale automated SMS weather advisories in local languages linked to satellite pasture and water point tracking tools.

internet_usage.name: Internet Usage Prevalence (%)
internet_usage.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 4 & p. 9
internet_usage.official_definition: Internet usage: percentage of women and men age 15–49 who have used the internet in the 12 months preceding the survey.
internet_usage.numerator: Population age 15–49 reporting internet access in the past 12 months.
internet_usage.denominator: Total population age 15–49 in the survey.
internet_usage.directionality_rationale: Internet connectivity facilitates market price discovery and online early warning information access.
internet_usage.climate_relevance: Low internet penetration means web-only portals fail to reach rural communities; human intermediaries remain vital.
internet_usage.guidance: Channel digital climate intelligence through ward agricultural officers, chiefs, and community radios rather than web portals alone.

radio_access.name: Radio Access (Early Warning Channel) (%)
radio_access.source_document: KNBS (2019) Kenya Population and Housing Census Volume IV: Socio-Economic Characteristics
radio_access.official_definition: Proportion of private households reporting ownership and functional use of a radio receiver.
radio_access.numerator: Households possessing an operational radio receiver.
radio_access.denominator: Total enumerated private households in the county.
radio_access.directionality_rationale: Radio is the most equitable, cost-effective, and vernacular medium for broad-scale early warning dissemination.
radio_access.climate_relevance: Pastoralist communities heavily tune in to vernacular FM radio broadcasts during seasonal migration cycles.
radio_access.guidance: Sponsor weekly airtime on local vernacular radio stations for KMD County Directors of Meteorology.

grid_electricity.name: Grid Electricity Connection Rate (%)
grid_electricity.source_document: KNBS (2019) Kenya Population and Housing Census Volume IV: Socio-Economic Characteristics
grid_electricity.official_definition: Proportion of conventional households using national grid electricity as their main source of lighting.
grid_electricity.numerator: Households connected to the national electrical grid.
grid_electricity.denominator: Total conventional households in the county.
grid_electricity.directionality_rationale: Grid connectivity underpins commercial agro-processing, cold-chain storage, and industrial water pumping.
grid_electricity.climate_relevance: Extremely low grid connectivity across pastoral settlements renders centralized electric pumping impossible.
grid_electricity.guidance: Mandate dedicated solar PV arrays for all community borehole water pumping and livestock market lighting.

solar_home.name: Solar Home Lighting Access (%)
solar_home.source_document: KNBS (2019) Kenya Population and Housing Census Volume IV: Socio-Economic Characteristics
solar_home.official_definition: Proportion of conventional households using decentralized solar photovoltaic systems (solar lanterns, home kits, solar panels) as primary lighting source.
solar_home.numerator: Households utilizing off-grid solar equipment for lighting.
solar_home.denominator: Total conventional households in the county.
solar_home.directionality_rationale: Decentralized solar adoption demonstrates community acceptance of clean, off-grid renewable energy technologies.
solar_home.climate_relevance: Provides existing private distribution networks capable of deploying productive-use solar refrigeration and milling.
solar_home.guidance: Leverage private off-grid solar networks to deploy productive-use solar refrigeration and pasture hammer milling equipment.

road_access.name: All-Weather Rural Road Access Index (%)
road_access.source_document: Kenya Rural Roads Authority (KeRRA) / KNBS Statistical Abstract (2024)
road_access.official_definition: Rural Access Index (SDG indicator 9.1.1): proportion of the rural population living within 2 kilometres (approximately 20 minutes walking distance) of an all-season motorable road.
road_access.numerator: Rural population residing within 2 km buffer of classified all-weather roads.
road_access.denominator: Total rural population in the county.
road_access.directionality_rationale: All-weather road access ensures reliable commodity transit, commercial destocking, and humanitarian emergency access.
road_access.climate_relevance: Unpaved earth roads become impassable during seasonal rains, cutting off food transport and triggering acute price spikes.
road_access.guidance: Prioritize gravel surfacing, vented drifts, and box culverts on key economic corridors connecting rural markets to the Isiolo–Moyale corridor.

bank_mobile_money.name: Commercial Bank / Mobile Money Access (%)
bank_mobile_money.source_document: KNBS (2025) County Gender Data Sheet, p. 4 & p. 9
bank_mobile_money.official_definition: Ownership and use of mobile phones and bank accounts: percentage of women and men who have and use an account in a bank or other financial institution, or use a mobile phone for financial transactions.
bank_mobile_money.numerator: Adults with registered commercial bank, SACCO, or mobile money accounts.
bank_mobile_money.denominator: Total adult population age 18+ in the county.
bank_mobile_money.directionality_rationale: Formal financial inclusion enables household cash savings, digital remittance flows, and index-based insurance claim payouts.
bank_mobile_money.climate_relevance: Pastoralists without financial accounts cannot receive direct digital cash transfers during sudden climate disaster onset.
bank_mobile_money.guidance: Expand liquidity support for rural cash-merchant agents in pastoral centers ahead of anticipated cash transfer disbursements.

ew_alert_timeliness.name: Early Warning Alert Timeliness (%)
ew_alert_timeliness.source_document: National Drought Management Authority (NDMA) Early Warning Bulletins / KNBS (2023)
ew_alert_timeliness.official_definition: Proportion of community respondents receiving seasonal weather forecasts and climate hazard early warning advisories at least 3 weeks prior to seasonal rainfall onset.
ew_alert_timeliness.numerator: Surveyed households receiving actionable climate advisories with >=3 weeks lead time.
ew_alert_timeliness.denominator: Total households surveyed in the county early warning sample.
ew_alert_timeliness.directionality_rationale: Adequate lead time is essential for pastoralists and farmers to procure inputs, adjust herd migration routes, or execute destocking.
ew_alert_timeliness.climate_relevance: Alerts arriving after seasonal onset leave communities unable to protect livestock assets or purchase drought seeds.
ew_alert_timeliness.guidance: Institutionalize automated SMS alert triggers directly linking KMD seasonal forecasts to community radio broadcasts and chief barazas.
